newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise further ahead of rating.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise further ahead of rating.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose further on Thursday ahead of the forthcoming announcement of Russia's country debt rating for its Eurobond issue, but then eased, meeting support at new levels, dealers said.

Finance minister Alexander Livshits said on Tuesday that the rating should be known in the next 10 days. Dealers said previously some Western operators were expecting the announcement today or on Friday.

"The market seemed short of paper in the morning as buying interest was active. Everybody is waiting for the news concerning the rating... Trading is quiet now as shorts seem to be covered," a Western bank dealer said.
A Mezhkombank dealer said the market was also anticipating positive news about President Boris Yeltsin's health.
"Recently he has been shown on TV more often... There are no bad news (about Yeltsin) while good news is likely."
Dealers said prices had risen on a mixed speculative and investor interest both from Russia and abroad.
They added the most actively traded shorter three papers eventually edged down from resistance levels of 79.50, 55.50 and 37.50 respectively.
